title: Near-miss negatives leak held-out numbers into training
description: Phase-(b) near-miss augmentation draws d2p = rng.integers(0,10) and appends a composite with label d1*10+d2p, with NO exclusion of held_numbers. assert_split_coverage guarantees every pos1 digit appears in HELD, so near-miss composites can equal held-out numbers. With shuffle_pairs=False the visual and audio composites at the same batch index share that label, so the held-out number is trained as a labeled cross-modal SupCon POSITIVE pair. Held-30 metrics are therefore contaminated and a positive compositional-generalization result cannot be distinguished from memorization - the exact failure mode the docstring (16-18) claims to exclude.
evidence: d2p = int(rng.integers(0, 10)); specs.append((d1, d2p)); labels.append(d1 * 10 + d2p)   # shares pos1
fix: Reject-sample d2p so that d1*10+d2p is not in held_numbers (or give near-miss items a label outside the evaluated number space), and assert generated near-miss labels are disjoint from held before training.

title: held-30 whole-number chance level mislabeled (actual 1%, documented 3.33%)
description: The docstring states 'chance 1.0% all-100 / 3.33% held-30', but run_one_model builds number prototypes over ALL present numbers (Pa/ua = number_protos over train+held) and retrieves held-mask queries against that full 100-number pool. Chance for held-30 is therefore 1/100 = 1%, not 1/30 = 3.33%. The verdict threshold wn_held>2.0 is interpreted against the wrong baseline, and the empirical perm null (~1%) contradicts the documented 3.33%.
evidence: Pa, ua = number_protos(aZ, a_lab)  # all present numbers; r = whole_number_retrieval(vZ[mask], v_lab[mask], Pa, ua, ...)
fix: Either restrict the held-30 retrieval pool to the 30 held prototypes (then 3.33% is correct) or fix the docstring/threshold to 1% chance; make the retrieval pool explicit in code and report.

title: Visual 'spike_rate'/'sparsity' is a post-conv2+ReLU activation rate, not a spike rate
description: _report_spiking_stats treats the stem output as summed spikes, but VisualMapStem.forward returns F.relu(conv2(time-summed LIF spikes)) - conv2 is a non-spiking real-valued refiner, so its tokens are ReLU activations, not spikes. counts=tokens.sum(-1)/T thus reports an activation magnitude mislabeled as spike_rate/sparsity for the visual modality. AudioMapStem returns genuine LIF spikes (s3), so the audio channel is correct; only visual is mislabeled. CLAUDE.md requires accuracy to travel with a genuine spike-rate/sparsity + timestep cost, so a mislabeled cost metric violates the integrity rule.
evidence: VisualMapStem.forward: m = F.relu(self.conv2(acc)); return m.flatten(2).transpose(1,2)  -> not spikes
fix: Measure the visual spike rate at the LIF output (s1 inside VisualMapStem) rather than after conv2/ReLU, or rename the visual column to conv2_activation_rate and stop reporting it as spike_rate/sparsity.

title: Per-digit horizontal jitter is inert for the right digit and boundary-violating for the left
description: Per-digit jitter is far weaker than the boundary comment implies. The RIGHT digit is fully inert: with RIGHT_X0=40 and the min/max clamp, xr==40 for every jitter in [-3,3]. The LEFT digit does jitter but only over xl in {0,1,2,3} (LEFT_X0=0, JITTER=3), spanning cols [3,37); it clips ~3px into the 6px inter-digit buffer (cols 34-39) but never reaches the right region (col>=40). The code's boundary comment is technically violated, but by ~3px, not by a large cross-region slide.
evidence: RIGHT_X0=40 + clamp => xr==40 for all jitter; LEFT_X0=0, JITTER=3 => xl in {0..3}, span [3,37), max 3px into the 6px buffer
fix: Make the augmentation actually jitter both digits within intended bounds (the right digit is pinned; the left moves <=3px); if a buffer-crossing near-miss is intended, widen the left range deliberately and assert it.

title: 'shuffled' negative control is defined inconsistently across phases
description: Phase (a) applies ONE permutation to a single label vector reused for both modalities (lab -> cat([lab,lab,lab,lab])), preserving cross-modal pairing while breaking the label-to-data correspondence. Phase (b) shuffles the AUDIO labels with an INDEPENDENT permutation (lab_a) while visual keeps lab, which breaks the cross-modal pairing itself. The negative control therefore means two different things across the curriculum, muddying its interpretation as a baseline.
evidence: phase a: if shuffle_pairs: lab = lab[torch.randperm(...)]  vs  phase b: lab_a = lab[torch.randperm(...)]
fix: Choose a single shuffle semantics (e.g. permute the cross-modal correspondence, or permute labels-vs-data) and apply it identically in both phases.

title: Aggregation double-counts a seed when a timestamped rerun CSV coexists with its base
description: load_rows_from_disk globs model_*_seed*.csv, which matches both model_X_seedN.csv and the model_X_seedN__<ts>.csv variant that _model_csv_path writes when the base already exists. write_summary_and_report means over ALL rows with no collapse to unique (model,seed), so a rerun inflates n_seeds and corrupts mean/std - the same near-duplicate inflation documented for generate_figures_3seed in CLAUDE.md.
evidence: for p in sorted(RESULTS_DIR.glob('model_*_seed*.csv')): ... ; vals = [r[key] for r in sub ...]  # no unique-seed collapse
fix: Collapse to one row per (model, seed) (keep the latest timestamp) before aggregating, and warn when duplicates are found.

title: assert_split_coverage can fail for arbitrary seeds and is then silently swallowed per-seed
description: assert_split_coverage requires all ten digits to appear in pos1 AND pos2 within BOTH the 70-number train set and the 30-number held set. A random 30/70 permutation split does not guarantee full per-position coverage for every seed. On failure the assert raises, and main's broad try/except prints a traceback and drops that seed, so a nominal 3-seed run can silently become fewer seeds.
evidence: assert p1 == set(range(10)), f'{name} missing pos1 digits: ...'  (raised inside run_one_model, caught by main)
fix: Resample the split in make_split until coverage holds (loop), or restrict to seeds verified to satisfy coverage; do not rely on the broad except to hide coverage failures.

title: Module-level pickle-alias hack mutates sys.modules['__main__'] at import time
description: At import, the module injects CachedNMNIST/CachedSHD/SubsampledByClass into sys.modules['__main__'] so torch.load(weights_only=False) of caches pickled under __main__ resolves. This is an import-time side effect (namespace pollution of whatever program imports this file) duplicated verbatim from run_joint_diagnostic.py:67-74. It only helps if the cache was pickled while run_joint_magnitude_ablation ran as __main__; no cache exists in-repo, so it currently guards a state that cannot occur until the magnitude script is first run as main.
evidence: for _cn in ('CachedNMNIST','CachedSHD','SubsampledByClass'): setattr(sys.modules['__main__'], _cn, getattr(_mag_module,_cn))
fix: Rebuild caches so the classes resolve to the importable run_joint_magnitude_ablation module, or load via a custom Unpickler that maps __main__.<cls> -> the module class; remove the __main__ mutation and factor the shared logic into one importable helper.

title: Running with no cache silently triggers a ~23 GB tonic render/download
description: _build_modality_loaders renders N-MNIST and SHD from tonic when the cache is absent; no results/ cache exists in this repo. The module comment claims it 'loads the existing 4.5 GB cache without a re-render', which is false in current repo state. The __main__ guard means import is safe, but an unsuspecting explicit run starts the full multi-hour render/download rather than a quick diagnostic.
evidence: loaders, cached = _build_modality_loaders(cfg)  # renders from tonic when cache missing (magnitude:174-198)
fix: Fail fast with a clear message if the cache directory is missing rather than silently rendering, and document the dataset prerequisite in the docstring.

title: Eval composites use TRAIN-set exemplars and differ across models
description: CompositeBuilder samples digit exemplars from cached['nmnist_train']/['shd_train'], and eval reuses the same builder whose RNG (seed+7) has been advanced by a model-specific amount of training (compositional 2 phases, holistic 1, untrained 0). So the four models are evaluated on different exemplar draws, cross-model comparison is not on identical inputs, and no unseen-EXEMPLAR generalization is tested (only unseen combinations).
evidence: builder = CompositeBuilder(cached, np.random.default_rng(seed + 7)); ... ev = extract_2digit(model, builder, device, ...)
fix: Use a separate fixed-RNG builder for evaluation, independent of training draws, and snapshot the eval spec list so every model sees identical inputs; consider held-out exemplars for a stronger test.

title: within_set_visual/within_set_audio columns are always NaN
description: run_one_model initializes within_set_visual/audio to NaN and never assigns them; within_modality_gate returns only 'loo' with a comment that within-modality SET is 'not available here'. These two CSV columns are dead in every output row.
evidence: 'within_set_visual': float('nan'), 'within_set_audio': float('nan')  # never set; gate returns only {'loo': ...}
fix: Either implement within-modality SET or remove the two columns from CSV_COLUMNS and the row dict.

title: Unused locals and a stale whole_number_retrieval docstring
description: d = slots.shape[2] is computed but unused in set_order_metrics (683) and _set_perm_null (712). whole_number_retrieval's docstring describes same-modality LOO handled 'by caller', but the function is only ever called cross-modally (vZ vs Pa, aZ vs Pv), so that path never runs; within-modality LOO is done separately in within_modality_gate.
evidence: d = slots.shape[2]  # unused;  docstring: 'LOO handled by caller ... when same-modality' (never same-modality)
fix: Delete the unused d locals; correct the whole_number_retrieval docstring to state it is cross-modal only.

title: File is a structural clone of run_joint_diagnostic.py and the magnitude harness
description: set_seed, _build_cfg, _mean/_std, _binom_z, load_rows_from_disk, write_summary_and_report, _report_spiking_stats, and the main/aggregate scaffolding are near-duplicates of run_joint_diagnostic.py and run_joint_magnitude_ablation.py. The two audited files together are ~95 KB of largely copy-pasted experiment harness, so a fix to one (e.g. the dedup or the spike-metric bug) must be applied in several places.
evidence: set_seed(146), _build_cfg(153), _mean/_std(969), _binom_z(979), load_rows_from_disk(953), write_summary_and_report(984) duplicate the sibling
fix: Extract a shared, importable, __main__-guarded harness module (seed, cfg, aggregation, spiking-stats) and import it from both experiment scripts.

title: _build_cfg populates ~30 fields but only 3 are consumed
description: _build_cfg constructs a full tri-modal/Hopfield/replay/align ExperimentConfig, but this file uses cfg only via get_device(cfg) (device) and _build_modality_loaders(cfg) (nmnist_train_per_class, batch_size). cfg.max_epochs/lr/patience are IGNORED - the real training budget is the module constants PHASE_A_EPOCHS/PHASE_B_EPOCHS/lr=1e-3 hardcoded in train_compositional. The sidecar even records lr=1e-3 as a literal, not from cfg. Editing cfg silently has no effect on training, which is misleading.
evidence: _build_cfg sets beta/dropout/num_patterns/num_gru_layers/align_*/... none used; train_compositional hardcodes lr=1e-3
fix: Reduce _build_cfg to the fields actually consumed, and source the sidecar values from the real constants.

title: Verdict thresholds are hardcoded magic numbers, only partly pre-registered
description: The auto-verdict uses order>60, wn_held>2.0, asym<5, set_v2a>set_perm+1.0 as decision cutoffs embedded in code. report.txt lists the metrics as 'PRE-REGISTERED' but not these numeric thresholds. Docstring chance values (37-42) are analytic claims and 'Procrustes ~0%' (8) is an unsourced prior result (RULE 1: no CSV in repo).
evidence: if clears_null and order > 60 and wn_held > 2.0 and asym < 5 and beats_holistic: verdict.append('FACTORIZES: ...')
fix: Promote thresholds to named constants and record them in the pre-registration block and the config sidecar; mark 'Procrustes ~0%' as an unsourced prior observation.

title: Runtime subprocess call to git for provenance
description: main shells out to `git rev-parse HEAD` to stamp the config sidecar. It is benign and wrapped in try/except (falls back to 'unknown'), noted only for the safety inventory (subprocess exec).
evidence: sha = subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'], cwd=REPO_ROOT).decode().strip()
fix: No action required; optionally read the SHA via a library or guard cwd existence.

title: Import chain is heavy but import-safe
description: Importing this file transitively imports run_joint_magnitude_ablation -> run_correspondence_anchor_v2 -> m7_trimodal_run_provenance, plus Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader, tonic and snntorch. All have __main__ guards and none load datasets at import, so importing does not start a run - but it is not free and pulls the whole magnitude/provenance stack. (Audited as text only; do not import to test.) snntorch/tonic/torch/numpy are all present in code/requirements.txt.
evidence: from run_joint_magnitude_ablation import (...); import snntorch as snn; (magnitude imports tonic + Dataloaders + run_correspondence_anchor_v2)
fix: No action required; if a lighter import is wanted, split the reused loaders/stems into a data-only module without the anchor_v2 dependency.

title: 'Above chance' verdict rests on a binomial z that treats correlated per-sample retrievals as independent
description: _binom_z uses n = n_vis_heldout (all N-MNIST test 6-9 samples, on the order of thousands) as independent Bernoulli trials, and _above_chance thresholds z>6. But every query is scored against the same set of prototypes with the same argmax structure, so the trials are strongly correlated (pseudo-replication); the binomial SE is understated and z is inflated. With n in the thousands, an accuracy only slightly above 10% (roughly 13%) already clears z>6, so weak structure reads as 'clearly above chance'. This statistic directly drives the written verdicts about a classifier-leak mechanism and the absence of emergent cross-modal generalization.
evidence: se = (p0*(1-p0)/max(n,1))**0.5; return (p_hat-p0)/(se+1e-12);  _above_chance: n=int(r.get('n_vis_heldout',0)); z>z_min(6.0)
fix: Use a test that accounts for correlation across shared prototypes (per-class or per-prototype resampling, or the permutation null with a robust spread) instead of equating sample count with independent trials; at minimum report the effective n and stop treating n_vis_heldout as the trial count.

title: legacy_untrained_v2a is computed via a full test-set forward but never analyzed; legacy_proto_a2v is written but never read
description: run_one_diagnostic_cell computes legacy_untrained = compute_held_out_metrics(untrained, ...), a full two-modality embedding pass over the N-MNIST and SHD test sets, solely to populate the legacy_untrained_v2a column, which no summary or report consumes. legacy_proto_a2v is likewise written to every CSV row but never read. Only legacy_proto_v2a is actually used (the artifact-collapse cross-check). So part of the legacy_* surface is dead code plus a wasted expensive forward pass per cell.
evidence: legacy_untrained = compute_held_out_metrics(untrained, loaders, device=device)  -> stored at 416, never read; legacy_proto_a2v stored at 415, never read
fix: Drop legacy_untrained_v2a and its forward pass and legacy_proto_a2v (or actually consume them); add a comment that legacy_proto_v2a is the degenerate 4-class metric kept only as an artifact cross-check, not a result.

title: The 2x2 SHARED-vs-SEPARATE design correctly isolates classifier-induced z-alignment (positive note)
description: Retrieval is measured on encoder embeddings z (per_sample_retrieval and compute_held_out_metrics both call model.embed), not on classifier logits. In the SHARED cell the phase-2 within-modality CE backpropagates through the single shared_classifier for BOTH modalities, so the shared head induces cross-modal alignment of the 6-9 embeddings with no cross-modal supervision - a valid positive control for the leak mechanism, absent in the SEPARATE cell. The new per-sample retrieval with TRAIN prototypes (282-333) is a genuine improvement over the transductive quantized 4-class metric it replaces. Recorded as an integrity-positive; no fix.
evidence: SharedHeadJointModel.forward uses one shared_classifier; train_model_diag Pass 2 (204-213) CE through it for both modalities; retrieval uses model.embed (z)
fix: No action required.
